subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What should the trust boundary and default activation policy be for plugin/agent/external recurring cron jobs that can spend model quota?
rationale: A mechanical fix would change public cron behavior, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, and upgrade behavior, so maintainers need to choose the intended safety boundary before implementation.

options.title: Provenance-gated scheduling API
options.body: Create or harden a scheduling path that records non-forgeable origin, requires approval or disabled-by-default activation for recurring non-operator jobs, and requires explicit model/cost policy before execution.

options.title: Default external jobs disabled
options.body: Make plugin/agent/external recurring cron registrations inactive until the operator enables them, accepting a compatibility migration and UX cost for existing automation.

options.title: Keep auto-enable with spend guards
options.body: Preserve current activation behavior but add budget/quota/cost circuit breakers and warnings, leaving consent and provenance weaker than the issue requests.

recommendation.title: Provenance-gated scheduling API
recommendation.body: Create or harden a scheduling path that records non-forgeable origin, requires approval or disabled-by-default activation for recurring non-operator jobs, and requires explicit model/cost policy before execution.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent cron/model-selection refactors put the active implementation surface closest to Vincent Koc, while the decision should still involve security/product owners.
